note: Candidates reviewed for this update but not admitted, with the reason and the evidence that would reopen each.

entries.candidate: Green Mountain LON-East campus, Romford: planned new data storage building and emergency energy centre at 5 King George Close ('LON2' expansion; Havering P1137.11 varied by P0614.20, section 73 application P1029.26 validated 28 August 2026)
entries.reason: The London Planning Datahub records Havering application P1029.26 (local gla/gla-Havering-P1029.26.json, sha256 e0be72c7...), validated 28 August 2026 and undecided, to vary conditions of P0614.20 (14 January 2021) for a new data storage warehouse and emergency energy centre on the former Hubbinet Industrial Estate at 5 King George Close, about 160 m south-east of the existing building. The Environment Agency's 29 April 2026 inspection report calls it a future 'LON2' expansion with four data halls and twelve engines, and Green Mountain's 1 September 2026 release says power and planning are secured for a further phase. It would be a second project on the LON-East site, but this fragment adds the site itself (the 14 MW expansion), and only one project can be added to a site that is new in the same update. Whether P0614.20 remains in effect (commenced or not) was not established, so permitted is not supported.
entries.reopen_condition: After the LON-East site is published, add the planned building as a project on that site reusing its campus locator exactly, as announced from P1029.26 while 28 August 2026 is within the window, or from a later Havering decision or Green Mountain statement; permitted needs evidence that the consent is in effect.

entries.candidate: Green Mountain LON-East campus, Romford: legacy 7 MW data-centre operations in the existing building (since 2010)
entries.reason: Green Mountain's explicit statement that '7 MW has been operational on the site since 2010' and that it will continue to operate the existing data centre is in its 8 June 2026 release, outside the 85-day window. The 1 September 2026 release calls LON-East 'an established 37 MW data center campus' and describes a customer that will occupy the newly delivered capacity, which does not explicitly state current operation (the Global Switch and Kao Harlow precedents require an explicit present-tense statement). The Environment Agency's 29 April 2026 inspection is also outside the window.
entries.reopen_condition: A dated (within 85 days) Green Mountain or Environment Agency record that explicitly states the LON-East data centre operates; then add an existing-operations project on the LON-East site reusing its campus locator.

entries.candidate: Amazon 'Silverdale Estate Data Centre', Silverdale Road, Hayes UB3 3BL (Environment Agency MCP permit EPR/UP3526LC) - possible identity context for the Atlas Silverdale Road data centre record (Hillingdon 49261/APP/2024/2904)
entries.reason: The Environment Agency register (local ea/ea-registration-EPR-UP3526LC.json) lists a medium-combustion-plant permit registered 15 October 2025 to Amazon Data Services UK Limited for 'Silverdale Estate Data Centre, Silverdale Road, Hayes, UB3 3BL', with a site point (TQ1029679447; 51.5032, -0.412287) 35 m from the Atlas Silverdale locator but about 20 m outside the Datahub condition polygons for 49261/APP/2024/2904. The permit fits the permission's single emergency generator, but the Hillingdon register does not name the applicant and the permit could relate to a different building on the estate, so it is not attached as identity context and no operator role is added.
entries.reopen_condition: A Hillingdon, Environment Agency or Amazon record that ties EPR/UP3526LC or Amazon to 49261/APP/2024/2904 (for example a decision notice naming the applicant or a permit variation naming Unit 4); then attach it as identity context or an intended operator role.

entries.candidate: Iron Mountain LON-1, 724-729 Dundee Road, Slough (EA bespoke permit application EPR/LP3020MX/A001) - re-check
entries.reason: Unchanged from the thirty-fifth holds. The consultation page re-captured on 27 October 2026 (local eac/iron-mountain-lon1-consultation.html) lists exactly the same documents as the 22 October capture; the only document not discussed before, the Climate Change Agreement 'CCA3' activation cover letter (local eac/im-cca3-cover-letter.pdf), is dated 6 March 2026 and is outside the window (it also names an individual, who is not reproduced). No permit has been issued: the installations register has no EPR/LP3020MX registration. The present-tense operation statements remain those of the 30 June 2026 non-technical summary.
entries.reopen_condition: As in the thirty-fifth holds: a dated in-window record of LON-1's operation (the permit decision document for EPR/LP3020MX/A001 or an Iron Mountain statement naming LON-1).

entries.candidate: Telehouse Docklands: West 2 permit variation EPR/EP3507SL/V004 (EA consultation opened 22 September 2026; operator's request-for-information response dated 9 September 2026) - re-check of the existing Telehouse records
entries.reason: The 9 September 2026 response by Telehouse's consultant to the Environment Agency (local eac/telehouse-v004-rfi-response-20260909.pdf) discusses generator-testing limits for West 2 and the existing North, North 2, East, West and South buildings, but states neither that the existing buildings operate nor any construction stage for West 2. The West 2 record is already 'permitted' as of 30 September 2026, later than both the response and the 22 September consultation, and the existing-operations record already rests on the same variation's 28 July 2026 non-technical summary. No admissible newer status.
entries.reopen_condition: A dated record after 30 September 2026 of West 2 construction (or after 28 July 2026 of current campus operation), for example the Environment Agency's V004 decision document or a Telehouse statement.
